newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian justice minister resigns - officials.
newsitem.headline: Colombian justice minister resigns - officials.

text.p: Colombian Justice Minister Carlos Medellin, an outspoken supporter of calls for an end to the country's constitutional ban on extradition, resigned on Monday, government officials said.

They said Medellin, who has won high marks from the United States for pushing tough anti-drug laws through Congress since he took office early last year, announced his "irrevocable decision" to step down in a letter handed early Monday morning to President Ernesto Samper.

Spokesmen for both Medellin and Samper said the resignation had been widely expected since Medellin -- a firm proponent of cracking down on Colombia's criminal drug gangs -- was preparing to launch a bid for a congressional seat or to stand as the running-mate of presidential hopeful Carlos Lleras de la Fuente in elections next year.

There was no official word on who Samper would name to replace Medellin. But local radio reports said the president had chosen Alba Beatriz de Rergifo, a lawyer and his personal adviser on legal affairs.

Samper announced earlier this month, at the urging of Medellin and under intense U.S. pressure, that he would propose legislation to lift the constitutional ban on extradition of drug lords and other criminals introduced by Colombia's constituent assembly in 1991.

Politial analysts and diplomats say the government faces a long, uphill battle to win approval of the legislation, since most Colombians oppose extradition and drug barons have shown they can influence many legislators.
U.S. officials say that detention in a secure facility in the United States is what Colombia's powerful drug lords fear the most.
